text:
Jack Hughes ended it at 3:23 of overtime, snapping a wrist shot past Joseph Woll on a 34% chance, and it was the one thing in this game that went the way the play suggested. NJD beat PHI 3-2 after generating 4.41 expected goals to PHI's 1.86, which left them deserving the win in 86% of simulated replays.

The gap was widest in the second period, when NJD out-chanced PHI 1.76 to 0.68 in expected goals. Woll kept PHI in it, stopping 41 of 44 shots, about 1.4 goals better than the quality of those chances called for. Rasmus Ristolainen tipped in the opening goal at 11:12 of the first, and Dougie Hamilton answered late in the second. Travis Sanheim then put PHI ahead with a slap shot at 5:33 of the third, a 4% chance that was the least likely goal of the night. Luke Hughes tied it at 9:44, assisted by Luke Evangelista.

Even in overtime, PHI had one real look. Trevor Zegras got a 43% chance, but Jake Allen stopped him. Moments later Jack Hughes, who played 25:48, scored off a Jesper Bratt feed. Bratt finished with six shots on goal and an on-ice expected goals split of 2.11 for to 0.27 against. PHI blocked 32 shots to NJD's 10 and lost the shot attempt count 95 to 41, which is how a team gets outplayed this badly and still reaches overtime.
